findings.title: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
findings.summary_md: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported that threat actors were using the ARTEX agentic framework to search public GitHub repositories for exposed secrets, including OAuth application credentials and AI service API keys, then use them against cloud tenants. Starting in August 2026 the agents sent high volumes of targeted GitHub queries; in one observed case an agent moved from finding a client secret to exfiltrating data from Azure Key Vault in five minutes. Microsoft also saw service principal sign-ins from 199.19.77[.]84 as early as October 28, 2026, and advised revoking or rotating exposed credentials rather than only deleting the source code.

findings.title: ARTEX: Agentic Asbestos
findings.summary_md: Censys counted 1,465 hosts serving an exposed ARTEX console as of November 4, 2026, about 815 of them distinct-looking deployments after removing two identically configured hosting blocks. It found 155 ARTEX hosts also running another Censys-detected threat, 32 open directories on ARTEX hosts, and a default console port of 8787/tcp. Censys scan history showed an open directory on the host named in the South Korean finance case from August 18, 2026, seven weeks before that report was published.

findings.title: Hacking on Autopilot: Inside ARTEX Cybercrime Campaigns
findings.summary_md: Check Point Research analyzed operator-side artifacts from ARTEX deployments and found 2,557 systems hosting or having hosted ARTEX panels, with 1,608 live public instances at the time of research; ten instances exposed the full ARTEX database. The exposed databases showed operators mostly using Chinese LLMs, including DeepSeek Flash models, for campaigns aimed at cryptocurrency theft, code-signing certificate theft, gaming credentials and denial of service. Check Point noted guardrails appearing only with Anthropic's Opus 5.5, after which an operator switched to more permissive models.

findings.title: ARTEX: AI Agents Find and Abuse Exposed GitHub Secrets
findings.summary_md: GitGuardian summarized Microsoft's ARTEX reporting and argued the exposed-secret problem predates the tool: its State of Secrets Sprawl 2026 counted 28.65 million new hardcoded secrets in 2025 and found 64% of valid secrets leaked in 2022 still active in 2026. The post described two unauthenticated checks, GET /api/health and GET /api/auth/status, that identify an ARTEX console and whether first-run setup is complete. It cited roughly 1,400 exposed instances from Censys as of November 4 and more than 1,800 from Check Point on November 5, noting the two counts use different methods.

findings.title: Beyond ARTEX: 45 AI Pentesting Tools and How to Find Them
findings.summary_md: GitGuardian cataloged about 45 open-source agentic penetration-testing frameworks around ARTEX, sorting 32 of them into five families. Only four shipped a secret scanner wired to the agent, and none included a GitHub fetcher, leaving the model to assemble the rest at runtime. The post matched the ARTEX family to 1,428 Shodan services on November 7, 2026, and noted 102 forks and ARTEX-named repositories appeared in the week of the October 8 takedown.

findings.title: ARTEX finds leaked secrets without a scanner: lab test
findings.summary_md: GitGuardian ran an ARTEX build in a sealed lab against a fake GitHub repository with nine planted credentials and found eight of them without any secret-scanning tool. The model improvised the hunt with git log --all, git show and grep, starting 6 to 13 seconds into the task, and did the same under a neutral prompt that never mentioned secrets. Only two of the nine canaries were in files at HEAD; the model recovered an AWS key deleted one commit after it was added, and it made no attempts to use any credential it found.
